title: ValueFormat
description: How a data widget formats the numbers it shows: the value type, for a duration its unit, for a currency its code, and optionally a fixed or a largest number of fraction digits, for a duration its two largest parts and, for a number, a unit word. percent 0.25 means 25%. Closed: no other field.

unit.description: The unit of a duration value: milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or days. Required when value_type is duration; not allowed otherwise.

compound.description: Optional, for a duration only. When true, the value shows as its two largest whole parts with narrow unit labels: 52 h shows as 2d 4h and 90 s as 1m 30s. The first part is the largest unit the value reaches at the precision the smaller units would show it: a day in whole minutes, an hour or a minute in whole seconds, a second in whole milliseconds; a value that reaches no second shows in whole milliseconds, and one that rounds to no millisecond shows as 0 in its own unit, such as 0h. So 23.5 h shows as 23h 30m, 59.6 s as 1m and 600 ms as 600ms. Each part rounds to the precision of the part after it and carries, so 47.9 h shows as 2d; from one second up the smallest part is seconds, so 1500 ms shows as 2s and 999.6 ms as 1s. A part has no group separator: 1234.5 d shows as 1234d 12h. A negative value carries its sign on the first part only: -52 h shows as -2d 4h and -59.6 s as -1m. Not allowed with decimals or max_decimals when true: the parts are whole by definition. Without it, or when false, the value shows in its unit.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of a currency value, such as EUR; the value is an amount in that currency. Required when value_type is currency; not allowed otherwise.

decimals.description: Optional exact number of fraction digits shown, for every value type. Not allowed with max_decimals or with compound true. Without decimals or max_decimals, a number shows up to three fraction digits, a percent up to two, and a currency the digits of its code.

max_decimals.description: Optional largest number of fraction digits shown, for every value type: each value shows only the fraction digits it needs, up to this number, so a whole value shows none. max_decimals 1 writes 47.25 as 47.3, -47.25 as -47.3 and 1234 as 1,234. A tick label on a chart's value axis is the tick rounded to this number, so labels can step unevenly: ticks at 0, 0.35, 0.7, 1.05 and 1.4 read 0, 0.4, 0.7, 1.1 and 1.4 with max_decimals 1. With max_decimals 0, the primary value axis of a cartesian chart draws whole ticks only, unless it shows percents (a percent value type, or stack_mode percent). Not allowed with decimals, nor with compound true.

unit_label.description: Optional unit word shown after a number, such as lines. Allowed with value_type number only. Without it, the number shows alone.
